description: How to place each SHARED_DENY_LIST entry into a REAL terraform plan.
The deny-list holds five kinds of thing and they do not carry their identity in
the same field. A service account is `.email`, and its `.name` is
`projects/-/serviceAccounts/<email>`. A bucket is `.name`. A cluster's `.id` is

`projects/

/locations//clusters/`, a network's is

`projects/

/global/networks/`, and Firestore's shared database is

`projects/

/databases/(default)`. Proving the guard catches a neighbour
therefore means copying the REAL resource_change of the matching type out of a
real plan and substituting the neighbour's identity into the fields the
provider actually populates -- not writing a fixture from memory.
WHY THIS IS A FILE AND NOT A CASE STATEMENT IN EACH READER. Two things need
this mapping: scripts/verify-destroy-guard.sh, which runs it against a live
plan, and tests/integration/test_destroy_guard_real_plan.py, which runs it
against the recorded one in CI. This repository has already paid for the
alternative three times over -- the deny-list transformation existed in three
spellings and the one inside `destroy.sh --self-test` had lost the `(default)`
entry, so the self-test of the guard protecting the shared Firestore database
could never reach that branch. A mapping with two implementations drifts the
same way.
`classify` is ORDERED and the FIRST match wins: a subnet must be reached by
`*subnet*` before anything broader sees it. The patterns use `*` only, because
that is the one wildcard every reader agrees on exactly.
The rules here are GENERIC: the kinds every deployment's names share (a service
account's address, Firestore's `(default)`, a `*-vpc`, a `*subnet*`) and the
placeholders the tests use. A deployment's own names are not in this
repository: its deny-list.json (gs://<state-bucket>/config/<env>/) carries its
own `classify` rules, which common.sh reads AHEAD of these.
AN ENTRY THAT MATCHES NOTHING IS A FATAL ERROR in the proof, never a skip.
The defect this whole exercise answers is a proof that silently covered
fourteen of twenty entries.
The inventory FLOORS are not here any more. A proof whose input is the list
it is proving can never notice the list getting shorter -- MEASURED: deleting
one service account from the list left this proof green -- so the floors are
asserted independently of the entries. They are deployment values, so they
moved into the same object as `floors` (kind -> minimum count, `total` for
all), and deny_list_load in common.sh refuses a list below any of them on
every load, not only when this proof runs. deny_list_floors prints them.
`patch` is a jq expression applied to that resource's `change.before`, with $e
bound to the deny-list entry and $p to the project id. `expect_matched` is what
the guard must PRINT as the reason it refused: the entry itself for a token
match, or the literal `default-network` for the bare `default`, which
`guard_deny_json` removes from the token list on purpose (the string appears
inside too many unrelated ids) and which destroy-guard.jq matches on the
network/subnetwork FIELD instead.
